text: A common online scam claims that the victim has won a prize, lottery, giveaway, or reward and asks for personal information or an upfront payment to receive it.
Investment scams often promise unusually high or guaranteed returns, create urgency to invest quickly, and may request cryptocurrency or direct transfers.
Tech support scams may falsely claim that a device is infected or compromised and pressure the victim to install remote-access software, provide credentials, or pay for unnecessary support.
Delivery scams may impersonate courier companies and claim that a package is delayed, requires a small payment, or needs address verification through a suspicious link.
Job scams may offer attractive employment opportunities and then request registration fees, equipment payments, personal documents, banking information, or other sensitive information.
Romance scams involve building trust or an emotional relationship before requesting money, financial assistance, gift cards, cryptocurrency, or other valuable resources.
Impersonation scams may pretend to be a friend, family member, manager, government official, bank employee, or another trusted person and request urgent financial or sensitive actions.
Refund scams may falsely claim that a payment was made incorrectly or that the victim is owed a refund, then request banking information, remote access, verification codes, or a transfer.
